text.tspan: Jacek Dobrzyniecki and Thomas Busch

flowRoot.flowPara: We investigate the competition between attractive spin-spin interactions and spin-separating external forces in the ground state of a one-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. We consider a lattice with open boundary conditions, subject to a linear external potential whose gradient β is opposite for the two spin components. We find that as β is increased, the bound pairs start breaking one-by-one, and three distinct regimes can be identified (pairs not broken, pairs partially broken, all pairs broken), separated by critical threshold gradients.
We also verify that this pair-breaking process persists under harmonic confinement. Our results are testable in cold-atom experiments.
• In this Hubbard model, tuning the potential gradient allows to precisely change the total number of bound pairs.
• There are direct relationships between the system parameters and the critical gradient threshold values.
• These results can be observed also in a lattice with harmonic confinement (easier to obtain in experiments than a box-like confinement).
Critical values of the gradient β
Counting the number of bound pairs

text.tspan: Finding the ground state: We use the Density Matrix
Renormalization Group (DMRG) numerical method
What determines the thresholds βc1, βc2: The critical
values of β depend directly on the system parameters. It's
even possible to derive approximate formulas that connect
βc1, βc2 to U, L, N (see our preprint for details).

tspan.tspan: Result of adding a harmonic trap:

text.tspan: We add a spin-independent harmonic
potential term with strength v:
Ground state for uniform system (β=0): The Bethe ansatz solution
says: all particles join up into N/2 bound pairs of opposite-spin fermions
Ground state for stronger gradient (β>0): As we increase β, the
bound pairs break, one by one — their constituent fermions move to the
lattice edges. The one-body densities, and the total doublon number,
change in abrupt jumps.
Critical values of β: βc1 — first pair breaks; βc2 — last pair breaks.
Therefore, three distinct regimes of β can be established.

flowRoot.flowPara: Doublon number and bound pairs: There is <1 doublon per bound pair. This ratio stays approximately unchanged, even as β is increased.
Counting the bound pairs: By rescaling the doublon number — so that it is equal to N/2 for β=0 — we can track the number of bound pairs as β is tuned.
The estimated pair number drops in integer plateaus.
(At small |U|, the pairs are extended over several sites, and they become looser with increasing β. The steps in ND are smoothed out)
